about.title: National City Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Defective products cause harm in ways that often go unrecognized until an injury happens — a faulty appliance in a home near E Plaza Boulevard, a malfunctioning tool used on a job site, or a vehicle part that fails while driving through National City. California law allows injured people to pursue claims against manufacturers, distributors, and retailers without needing to prove negligence, since strict liability generally applies once a defect and injury are shown. National City residents dealing with these situations often aren't sure who's actually responsible, especially when a product passed through several hands before reaching them. Our team provides a free consultation to help injured people in National City understand what happened and explore possible next steps, all without any upfront cost.

whyChoose.title: Why Product Liability Cases Work Differently

items.title: Strict Liability May Apply
items.desc: Under California law, you generally don't need to prove the manufacturer was careless — showing the product was defective and caused injury can be enough.

items.title: Multiple Parties Can Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers may all be liable depending on where the defect originated, which widens the paths toward accountability.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters
items.desc: Keeping the item involved, along with packaging or instructions, can be important — we can advise on how to protect that evidence.

items.question: Do I have to prove the company was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California generally allows strict liability claims for defective products, meaning you may only need to show the product was defective and that it caused your injury. We can review your situation and explain how this might apply.

items.question: What if the product was purchased outside National City?
items.answer: That's usually fine — what matters more is where the injury occurred and where you live now, both of which point to National City and San Diego County. Our team can sort out jurisdiction details for you.

items.question: Should I keep the product that injured me?
items.answer: Yes, if possible. Preserving the product, along with any packaging, receipts, or instructions, can be valuable as we evaluate your claim.
